findings.title: Consumer group rebalance shuts down the shared FixedQueuePool and causes all subsequent messages to be dropped and committed
findings.body: `ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__` creates a single `self.queue_pool = FixedQueuePool(...)` instance for the lifetime of the factory, and `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker()` passes that shared `self.queue_pool` into each `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` created by `create_with_partitions()`. In Arroyo, whenever a Kafka partition rebalance occurs, `StreamProcessor` closes or terminates the active `ProcessingStrategy` (`strategy.close()` / `strategy.join()` / `strategy.terminate()`) and then calls `factory.create_with_partitions()` for the new assignment. Because `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` and `terminate()` both call `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, the first rebalance permanently shuts down all queues (`q.shutdown()`) and exits all worker threads on `self.queue_pool`. On the new strategy created after the rebalance, every `submit()` call hits `work_queue.put()` on a shut-down queue, raising `queue.ShutDown`. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` catches `Exception`, logs it, and calls `add_offset()` + `complete_offset()`, so the consumer will silently drop 100% of messages after any rebalance while committing their offsets to Kafka. In addition, `self.queue_pool.offset_tracker` retains state from revoked partitions across rebalances, causing the commit thread to commit offsets for partitions the consumer may no longer own.

findings.title: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets skips over offset gaps after mark_committed prunes all_offsets
findings.body: In `OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets()`, the contiguous scan starts at `start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset)`. However, `mark_committed(partition, offset)` removes all offsets `<= offset` from `self.all_offsets[partition]`. As a result, once an offset has been committed, every remaining entry in `all_offsets` is strictly greater than `last_committed`, making `min_offset >= last_committed + 1` always true for monotonically increasing offsets. If there is a gap (e.g. offsets 100, 102, 103 are completed while 101 is still missing), the first call to `get_committable_offsets()` returns 100 and `mark_committed(partition, 100)` leaves `all_offsets = {102, 103}` and `last_committed = 100`. On the very next commit loop iteration, `min_offset` is 102, so `start = max(101, 102) = 102`, causing the tracker to jump over the missing offset 101 and commit 103. When `partition in self.last_committed`, `start` must be `self.last_committed[partition] + 1`, only using `min_offset` when no offset has been committed for that partition yet.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown abandons queued items and stops the commit thread before workers finish
findings.body:
There are two ordering defects in shutdown handling:
1. `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` sets `worker.shutdown = True` on all `OrderedQueueWorker` instances before calling `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. Because `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` loops on `while not self.shutdown:`, each worker exits immediately after finishing its current item instead of draining the remaining items in `self.work_queue` until `queue.ShutDown` is raised. Any queued items are abandoned with their offsets still in `offset_tracker.outstanding`.
2. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` sets `self.shutdown_event` and joins `self.commit_thread` *before* calling `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, with no final commit afterward. Offsets completed by workers while `queue_pool.shutdown()` is draining/joining are never committed to Kafka. (`SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.terminate()` also does not join `self.commit_thread`, and `ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown()` shuts down `queue_pool` without stopping `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.commit_thread`.)

findings.title: Worker queues are unbounded and provide no backpressure to Arroyo StreamProcessor
findings.body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy`'s docstring states that it provides "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but `FixedQueuePool.__init__` creates each `queue.Queue()` with the default `maxsize=0` (unbounded). Arroyo's `StreamProcessor` polls Kafka and calls `strategy.submit(message)` in a tight loop until `MessageRejected` is raised. Because `work_queue.put()` never blocks or rejects, if worker processing falls behind Kafka consumption, the consumer will buffer an unbounded number of `WorkItem` and `Message` objects in memory. Furthermore, if a bounded queue were used, the broad `except Exception:` handler in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit()` (lines 317-325) would catch `queue.Full` / `MessageRejected` and immediately mark the unqueued message's offset as completed instead of propagating `MessageRejected` to Arroyo.

findings.title: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling asserts the opposite of its docstring due to commit timer timing and leaks commit_thread
findings.body: `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` states "Test that errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages", and `OrderedQueueWorker.run()` calls `offset_tracker.complete_offset()` in its `finally` block even when `result_processor` raises an exception. However, the test exits its wait loop ~0.2s after the 2 items are processed (before `_commit_loop`'s 1.0s `shutdown_event.wait(1.0)` elapses) and asserts `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`—which asserts that offsets were *not* committed and will fail flakily if the test takes >1s on CI. In addition, the `test_thread_queue_parallel*` unit tests in `test_results_consumer.py` only call `factory.shutdown()` and never `consumer.close()`, leaving `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.commit_thread` running in the background after the tests finish.
